name: AI D7 - Why-now
description: Trigger line, discovery question, persona and proof for A/B accounts, from signal rows only.

parameters.content:
## D7 - Why-now for A/B
Structured signal rows in, Sonnet 5.5 at temperature 0 out: trigger_line (cheat-sheet format, facts only), discovery_q (picked from the product card), persona, proof (verbatim from the card), evidence_line, context. account_id echoed. An A with no usable trigger drops to B. Run after D6, before D8.

parameters.text:
=You write the first ten seconds of a cold call for an SDR at the company (global employment platform: EOR, contractor management, US PEO, Field Services for on-site crews, IT equipment for devices). Return ONLY the JSON requested.

account_id: {{ $json.account_id }} (return this exact value, unchanged)
Company: {{ $json.name }} ({{ $json.domain || "-" }}), {{ $json.headcount || "unknown" }} staff, industry {{ $json.industry || "unknown" }}, HQ {{ $json.hq_country || "unknown" }}
Band {{ $json.band }}, lead product: {{ $json.lead_product }}, conversation starter: {{ $json.convo_starter || "none" }}
Evidence summary: {{ $json.evidence_line || "-" }}
Score breakdown: {{ JSON.stringify($json.breakdown) }}
Open roles (last 90 days): {{ JSON.stringify($json.jobs) }}
News (last 9 months): {{ JSON.stringify($json.news) }}

COUNTRY RULE (applies to trigger_line and discovery_q)
- You may name a country or city ONLY if (a) an open role in that country appears in the Open roles list above, or (b) a news item above (expansion, new office, project win, acquisition) names that place. Those are the only proof of where they are hiring next.
- Staff already abroad, offices abroad and emp_abroad / offices_abroad in the breakdown are NOT hiring intent. Never name those countries. Describe them as "people in a few countries" or "a team spread across a few places".
- If neither a role nor a news item gives you a place, write the discovery question without one (patterns below have a no-country form).

FUNDING RULE
- A funding item with source "companies_house" (title starts "SH01 share allotment") is a raise seen on the public register that has not been announced. It is already checked: only real money reaches you. On the call it is subtext, never the headline, and the source is never named: no "Companies House", no "register", no "filing", no amount.
  - With a hiring signal (an open role, especially abroad): the role is the trigger and the round is a clause: "I saw you're hiring in Luxembourg and it looks like you've just closed a round, that's actually why I called."
  - With no hiring signal: "It looks like you've recently closed a round, that's actually why I called." Keep "it looks like".
- A funding item with source "news" is public: say it plainly with the amount if known ("I saw you've just raised £4m"). If both exist, use the news one.

DISTRIBUTED TEAM RULE
- Evidence containing "DISTRIBUTED TEAM (N countries, M staff)" or conversation starter "distributed" means a small company whose people sit in several countries with no real offices: almost always contractors, which is the vendor conversation itself. When it is the strongest signal (no raise in 90 days, no foreign role), the trigger line is: "I saw you've got a team of about [M] spread across a few countries, that's actually why I called." Round the headcount loosely ("about 20"). No country names, no count of countries.
- The discovery question is then the eor no-place staff-abroad pattern below ("How are the people outside the UK employed at the moment..."). Persona: founder under 50 staff.
- "new UK entity" in the evidence means a foreign-headquartered company that set up a UK company recently; it may be mentioned only in context and evidence_line, never on the call.

RULES FOR trigger_line
- Format: "I saw [specific thing], that's actually why I called." Under 25 words. ONE trigger, the strongest, in this order: a funding round in the last 90 days > foreign roles > distributed team / staff already abroad > expansion or project win > contract roles > US role > remote roles.
- If the company raised money in the last 90 days AND has foreign roles, join them in one line: "I saw you've just raised £4m and you're hiring in Lisbon, that's actually why I called."
- Staff already abroad as the trigger: "I saw you've got people in a few countries already, that's actually why I called." No country names.
- Only facts present above. Numbers, role titles, amounts (press only) and place names (subject to the country rule) are allowed; adjectives like fast-growing, exciting, impressive are not. Never mention the vendor in the trigger line.
- Signals older than 45 days are "recently", never "this week". If no fact above can carry a trigger line, return trigger_line as an empty string.

RULES FOR discovery_q
This is the ONE opening question after the trigger line. Tone: a mate helping a mate think through a complicated problem. Plain spoken, no jargon, no sales language, nothing the prospect could feel tested by. Answerable in one breath with a fact they already know, and either answer tells the SDR which conversation to have. The SDR is trained on the follow-ups, so do not add them. Under 25 words. British English.
Use the pattern for the lead product. Fill in [country] only under the country rule; otherwise use the no-country form. Keep the shape.
- eor, with a place from a role or news: "Is [country] going to be your first hire there, or have you done it before?"
- eor, no place but raised recently (press or register): "Where's the first hire going to be with the new money, is any of it outside the UK?"
- eor, no place, staff already abroad or distributed team: "How are the people outside the UK employed at the moment, own entity, contractors, or something in between?"
- contractors, with a place: "Are your contractors in [country] invoicing you direct, or do you run them through a platform?" No place: "Are your contractors abroad invoicing you direct, or do you run them through a platform?"
- contractors, agencies (evidence starts with "agency"): "When you place a contractor in [country], who holds the contract and runs the payments, you or the client?" No place: "When you place a contractor abroad, who holds the contract and runs the payments, you or the client?"
- us_peo: "Have you got a US entity already, and if so is payroll and benefits set up there yet?"
- field_services: "When you win a project somewhere you've no entity, how do you get the crew on the ground legally?"
- it_equipment, with a place: "How are you getting a laptop out to someone in [country], set up and secure, and back again when they leave?" No place: "How are you getting laptops out to people abroad, set up and secure, and back again when they leave?"
- If the conversation starter is immigration AND the lead product is eor: "Anyone you're trying to move across borders at the moment, and who's tracking the visa dates?"

persona: one of founder, hr, finance, ops. founder when under ~30 staff and no People/HR role appears in the roles, and always for a company that raised in the last 90 days with under 50 staff, and for a distributed team under 50 staff; hr when a People/HR/Talent role appears or the company is 30+ staff with an EOR lead; finance when lead is contractors; ops when lead is field_services or it_equipment.

proof: choose ONE verbatim by fit, or an empty string if none fits.
- "Customer A, scaled from 1 to 38 people across 7 countries with no in-house HR, 50+ contractors on one platform." (founder, contractor-heavy, small, distributed team)
- "Customer B, a SaaS scale-up that hired 50+ people across 14 countries through the vendor." (tech / SaaS hiring abroad)
- "Customer C, a UK fintech, hired 100 people they couldn't have otherwise and grew headcount 20% in a year." (fintech / scaling)
- "Customer D, cut contractor onboarding to a single day and saves up to $140k a year." (finance / contractor ops)
- "Customer E, got a full day a week of HR admin back and halved onboarding time." (HR / People lead)
- "Customer F, scaled hiring across five countries in weeks, not months." (ops / speed)
- "[vendor headline statistic]." (anything else)

evidence_line: one line, under 20 words, the facts behind the trigger, for the SDR's eyes only: for a register raise write "SH01 on register, unannounced" plus the amount if given; for a distributed team write "team in N countries, M staff" with the countries; roles, countries (any country may appear here), dates, headcount. No adjectives.
context: two sentences for the account executive's email sequence: what the signals add up to and which product conversation it is. May mention the vendor.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: {"account_id":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000","trigger_line":"I saw you have two engineering roles open in Lisbon, that is actually why I called.","discovery_q":"When you found those hires in Portugal, what was the plan for employing them, and what happens to the role if it takes four months to sort?","persona":"founder","proof":"Customer B, hired 50+ people across 14 countries through the vendor.","evidence_line":"2 roles Lisbon, posted 28 Sep · 38 staff · Software","context":"UK entity only, first foreign roles live since late September. Classic first international hire."}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_account_id: $json.output.account_id, p_trigger_line: String($json.output.trigger_line || "").split(/\s+/).slice(0, 30).join(" "), p_discovery_q: $json.output.discovery_q || "", p_persona: $json.output.persona || "", p_proof: $json.output.proof || "", p_evidence_line: $json.output.evidence_line || "", p_context: $json.output.context || "", p_model: "claude-sonnet-5-5" }) }}
